title: Evolving patterns of co-mutations from tumor initiation to metastatic progression.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded Zenodo record 13752870 (CC-BY-4.0): supplementary_data_2.tar (16.7 MB, 395 files) and supplementary_data_1.tar (3.4 MB, 115 files). Opened the pan-cancer R objects in R: each holds two binary gene-by-sample matrices (missense, truncating) over 396 OncoKB genes, a per-sample mutation count (TMB), and a tumour-subtype label. Counts seen: MSK primary 27,825 and metastatic 14,965 samples; DFCI (Dana-Farber) primary 14,657 and metastatic 7,607; TCGA 9,082 (all primary). Total 74,136. In MSK there are 67 subtype labels, no duplicate sample IDs and 0 patients shared between the primary and metastatic files. Values are 0/1 only. Oddity: on average a sample carries 1.12 oncogenic missense calls but 2.36 truncating calls, which looks suspicious. Listed the 615 MB analysis archive (record 16077065) without downloading it (over the 50 MB cap).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the mutations were curated as putatively oncogenic with OncoKB, that 119 subtypes exist across all cohorts, the MSK-MET metastasis-count elastic net (12,925 samples), and that primary versus metastatic status comes from the GENIE sample-type annotation. Panel-specific files and the GENIE per-centre files were not opened one by one.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo, open, CC-BY-4.0, no login; downloaded both tars. Raw GENIE needs a Synapse login, but the processed matrices here don't.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Primary versus metastatic sample is encoded by which file a sample sits in (separate primary/meta files per centre), so it is one concatenation away from a column. Tumour subtype is a named vector. Checked in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are the matrices themselves: 396 genes x 2 mutation types, plus TMB (tumour mutational burden). No lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Binary 0/1 mutation calls and an integer mutation count, so units aren't really an issue. The README documents the object layout.

a5_enough_rows.note: 42,790 MSK and 22,264 DFCI samples with primary/metastatic status, plus 9,082 TCGA primaries. Counted in the files.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: about 20 MB compressed; ~65k x 793 binary matrix, under 0.5 GB in RAM

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 74,136 samples counted, consistent with the paper's '>70,000 tumours'. The paper's '119 subtypes' wasn't verified across cohorts (MSK alone has 67).

a8_label_provenance.note: Primary/metastatic is a clinical annotation of where the biopsy came from (GENIE sample type), not computed from mutations. Caveat: the mutation features were filtered by OncoKB, a curated annotation, which is fine for features but bakes in OncoKB's choices.

B1.why: Few R objects per centre (primary and meta files) that join cleanly on sample ID; seen in files.

B2.why: RDS needs R or pyreadr to export; parsed first try in R.

B3.why: Same 396-gene OncoKB space, but MSK and DFCI use different panels; older panels lack some genes, which show up as structural zeros.

B4.why: Binary calls and integer counts, nothing censored; seen in files.

B5.why: 0 duplicate sample IDs and 0 patient overlap between MSK primary and meta files; checked.

B6.why: README explains object layout; missense/truncating averages look suspicious and gene-panel masking isn't documented per sample.

C1.why: MSK-to-DFCI transfer is informative either way, but a single-centre primary/metastatic score mostly repeats MetaNet.

C2.why: MetaNet (XGBoost, 32,176 samples), TF-GateNet and P-NET exist for this task; mostly random or within-cohort splits.

C3.why: Weak 'better' angle: cross-centre test, plus whether co-mutation features add over single genes.

C4.why: Metastasis status is known clinically; a prediction would only matter for risk stratification of primaries.

C5.why: Obvious baselines: tumour-type-only model and single-gene logistic regression; MetaNet reports AUROC >0.8 in breast and prostate.

D1.why: No pretrained backbone for binary cancer-gene panel profiles; gene embeddings would be decoration.

D2.why: Gradient boosting or logistic regression on CPU runs in minutes; no embeddings needed.

D3.why: Data are CC-BY-4.0; GENIE terms ask for acknowledgement.

E1.why: Held-out centre (train MSK, test DFCI) and held-out tumour type are both possible from the files.

E2.why: Two centres, 67 MSK subtypes; per-panel files give further groups.

E3.why: Tumour-type-only and TMB-only baselines are directly computable.

E4.why: No replicate biopsies of the same tumour; primary and metastatic files share no patients.

E5.why: Known treatment-driven enrichments in metastases (ESR1 in breast, AR in prostate; Nguyen 2022) must be recovered.

E6.why: Label shuffling within tumour type, and a panel-version-only model, are both runnable.

E7.why: The DFCI cohort is an independent centre with a different panel (OncoPanel).

E8.why: MetaNet's exact split isn't in this data; the paper's elastic net needs MSK-MET clinical counts in the 615 MB archive.

G1.why: HGNC gene symbols and GENIE sample IDs joinable to cBioPortal MSK-MET and MSK-CHORD.

G2.why: MSK-MET on cBioPortal adds metastatic-site counts and organotropism for the same MSK samples.

G3.why: One sample per row; GENIE-MSK-P-xxxx-T01 maps one-to-one to the cBioPortal sample ID.

G4.why: Joining adds metastatic sites, but site-tropism from MSK-IMPACT is already published.

H1.why: Both primary and metastatic samples present, roughly 2:1 in MSK; seen in files.

H2.why: Two US academic centres plus TCGA; panel sequencing only, no copy-number or fusion features in these objects.

H3.why: Claim is precise: separating biopsy site type from oncogenic panel mutations at US tertiary centres.

H4.why: Paper discusses panel heterogeneity; therapy-induced confounding of metastatic samples is only partly discussed.

I1.why: Ciriello lab and cancer-genomics groups; clinicians unlikely to act on a sample-type score.

I2.why: Might shape which co-mutations to test as metastasis risk factors; no direct clinical decision.

I3.why: AUROC per tumour type roughly matches risk-ranking, but the label is biopsy site, not future metastasis.

I4.why: Tumour type plus a few genes probably explains most signal; ML adds interactions.

J1.why: Real cross-centre evaluation and leakage work, but tabular gradient boosting, no transfer learning.

J2.why: Known gene enrichments give sanity checks; cancer-genomics expertise helps for confounding.

J3.why: Cleaned pan-centre table and transfer numbers are shareable even if the model is modest.

J4.why: Roughly two weeks; not formally set.

J5.why: Kill condition proposed below; date not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: MetaNet (Nature Communications 2021, 'Machine learning of genomic features in organotropic metastases stratifies progression risk of primary tumors')
existing_models.score_and_split: XGBoost on 32,176 MSK-IMPACT, FoundationOne, MET500 and TCGA samples; AUROC (area under the ROC curve) >0.8 for primary vs metastasis in breast and prostate; split details not checked.

existing_models.name: TF-GateNet (PMC13296772), a biologically constrained neural network
existing_models.score_and_split: Primary vs metastatic in prostate and breast on a fixed 80/10/10 random split over 10 runs, plus independent prostate external validation; numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract names cross-institution batch effects and gene-coverage differences in GENIE-like data.

existing_models.name: Deep learning on mutational signatures (Scientific Reports 2023) and the passenger-mutation classifier (Nature Communications 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Whole-genome-based primary vs metastatic classification; numbers not retrieved. Different input (whole genomes), so not directly comparable to panels.

backbone.name: none suitable (binary cancer-gene panel features; gradient boosting is the baseline)

integration.partner_dataset: MSK-MET (cBioPortal, ~25,000 patients with metastatic-site counts) and MSK-CHORD (treatments)
integration.join_key: GENIE sample ID with the 'GENIE-MSK-' prefix stripped (P-xxxxxxx-Txx-IMx)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do co-mutations found in primaries predict where and how much a cancer spreads, beyond treatment-induced mutations?

controls.positive_control: Recover known treatment-driven metastatic enrichments: ESR1 in hormone-receptor-positive breast and AR in prostate metastases (Nguyen et al. 2022).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the primary/metastatic label within tumour type; also train on panel version (IM3/IM5/IM6/IM7 suffix) alone to measure the leak.
controls.external_validation: Train on MSK, test on DFCI (Dana-Farber, a different centre and panel), both present in the downloaded files.

honest_claim_h3: Among tumours panel-sequenced at two US cancer centres, oncogenic mutation profiles distinguish biopsies taken from metastatic sites from primary-site biopsies to some degree, partly because of therapy-selected mutations; this isn't a prediction of whether a primary will spread.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the set of cancer-gene mutations in a tumour biopsy to predict whether it came from a metastasis or the original tumour.
plain_idea.train_on: For each tumour sample, yes/no calls for missense and truncating mutations in 396 cancer genes, plus mutation count and cancer subtype; 42,790 MSK samples (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the sample was taken from a metastatic site or the primary tumour, as recorded clinically in the AACR GENIE registry; tested on 22,264 Dana-Farber samples (verified).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Shows whether metastasis-linked mutation patterns carry over between hospitals with different gene panels, or are mostly centre and panel artefacts.

more_or_better_data.why: 42,790 MSK plus 22,264 DFCI labelled samples, against MetaNet's 32,176 across four sources; ours adds a second centre for transfer but is not much larger.

confidence_score.why: No replicate biopsies, so there is nothing to calibrate noise against beyond standard probability calibration.

models_beatable.why: MetaNet (2021, XGBoost) and TF-GateNet (random 80/10/10 split) aren't evaluated across centres here; but a strong gradient-boosting baseline is easy and leaves little room.

guaranteed_improvement.why: MetaNet's code and split aren't available in these files, and DFCI is a different panel, so the same-split, superset-data conditions fail.

label_elsewhere.sources: AACR GENIE full releases (sample type for all centres; Synapse login needed, known resource); MSK-MET on cBioPortal (open, same MSK patients; searched).
label_elsewhere.why: Other GENIE centres would allow testing transfer to more hospitals, but only behind a registration.

risks: Panel version (IM3 to IM7 in the sample ID) tracks sequencing date and gene coverage, and may correlate with how many metastases were biopsied.
Genes missing from older panels appear as 0, so 'not sequenced' looks like 'not mutated'.
Tumour subtype strongly predicts the metastatic fraction, so a model can score well by learning subtype alone.
Treatment-induced mutations (ESR1, AR) mark metastases because those patients were treated, not because the mutation drives spread.
leakage_plan.split: Train on MSK, test on DFCI (centre = which file, seen); within MSK, hold out whole tumour subtypes (sample.class vector, seen) and stratify by panel suffix in the sample ID (seen).
checks: Shuffle labels within subtype; AUROC must drop to the subtype-only baseline.
Train on panel suffix and subtype only, and report that as the floor to beat.
Repeat with genes restricted to those common to every panel and check the result holds.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable, but confounding by subtype, panel and treatment is the main risk and must be reported as a baseline.

success_criteria.metric: Mean per-subtype AUROC (area under the ROC curve) on DFCI after training on MSK, because subtype mixing otherwise inflates pooled AUROC.
success_criteria.baselines: Subtype-plus-TMB-only logistic model (to compute); MetaNet reports AUROC >0.8 in breast and prostate on its own split (not comparable).
success_criteria.success: Mutation model beats the subtype-plus-TMB baseline by ≥0.05 mean per-subtype AUROC on DFCI, with the gain surviving restriction to genes common to all panels.
success_criteria.kill: Gain under 0.02 AUROC over the subtype-plus-TMB baseline on DFCI after the first week.

ambitious.why: Publishes cross-cohort genomic benchmarks; would need a clear cross-centre transfer result plus co-mutation features adding real signal.

realistic.why: Takes modest clinical-genomics ML evaluations, such as an honest cross-centre test of metastasis classifiers.

fallback.journal: NAR Cancer or a bioRxiv preprint
fallback.why: A negative result, that panel and subtype confounding explain most of the signal, is still a useful short report.

pitch.headline: 74,136 tumour profiles in open CC-BY matrices, with 65,054 labelled primary or metastatic across two independent cancer centres.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Harmonised OncoKB-filtered calls for the same 396 genes at MSK (42,790) and Dana-Farber (22,264), so the raw GENIE Synapse login isn't needed and cross-centre transfer can be tested directly.
pitch.the_win: A mutation model beating the subtype-plus-TMB baseline by ≥0.05 per-subtype AUROC when trained on MSK and tested on Dana-Farber.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Quantifies how much published primary-vs-metastasis accuracy comes from subtype, panel version and treatment-selected mutations rather than biology.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Ciriello lab (SelectSim authors) and GENIE consortium analysts deciding whether pooled-centre metastasis signatures are trustworthy.

ml_idea: Concatenate the MSK and DFCI primary and meta run_data matrices into one sample-by-(396 genes x 2 types + TMB + subtype) table. Train gradient boosting on MSK and test on DFCI, comparing against a subtype-plus-TMB baseline and against added SelectSim co-mutation pair features.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the matrix sizes seen (about 65k samples x 793 binary features); nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fit subtype-plus-TMB-only and subtype-plus-panel-suffix models on MSK and test on DFCI; if adding mutations gains under 0.02 AUROC, stop.

verdict_reason: The data are clean, open and verified (74,136 samples, two centres), but primary-vs-metastasis prediction from panels is already done (MetaNet, TF-GateNet). No pretrained backbone fits, and the label is heavily confounded by subtype, panel and treatment, so the likely result is a modest benchmark note.
